title: Metaphysics I: existence, objects and persistence
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study the core of contemporary metaphysics about what there is: the aims and methods of metaphysics, existence and ontological commitment, universals and properties (realism, nominalism and tropes), abstract objects, substance and the bundle theory, material constitution, composition and the special composition question, persistence (endurance and perdurance), and personal identity.
primary_reading: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (free): entries on ontological commitment, properties, material constitution and temporal parts

weeks.1: What is metaphysics? Aims and methods
weeks.3: Universals and the problem of the one over many
weeks.5: Abstract objects: numbers and the epistemological challenge
weeks.7: Material constitution: the statue and the clay
weeks.10: Change and the problem of temporary intrinsics
weeks.11: Personal identity: psychological and biological views

blocks.deliverable: Find the ontological commitments of five sentences.
Compare realism and trope theory on one case.
Reconstruct the epistemological argument against platonism.
Week 7 midterm; evaluate three answers to the special composition question.
Explain how a perdurantist handles change.
Write a three-page essay on fission cases.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Metaphysics paper: write a 2,500-word paper on one puzzle from the course (the statue and the clay, the special composition question, the ship of Theseus, temporary intrinsics or fission) that states the puzzle precisely, compares two solutions with their costs, and defends one.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
